title: Why caching makes apps faster
learningObjective: Explain a cache miss, cache hit, reduced repeated work, stale data and explicit invalidation using a product-price lookup.

segments.text: Same app. Same price. Why is the second request faster?
The first request checks the cache. Nothing there. A cache miss.
So it fetches the price from the database. Twenty dollars.
The app saves a copy in the cache for later.
Ask again. The cache already has it. A cache hit. Less work, less waiting.
But copies can go stale. The database price changes to twenty five dollars.
The cache still says twenty. Fast, but wrong.
Here, we invalidate that old copy. The next request fetches and stores the new price.
That is caching. Reuse work you have already done, with a plan to keep it fresh.
